_readme: CAMPAIGN levels, in play order. Same knobs as sizes.json, plus teaching tips.
cont / types are per-room caps (how many containers, how many emoji each).
sizes.json instead uses targetTypes, a whole-run quota. Levels want tight
control of what one room shows; free play wants a total.
TIPS — one bubble at a time, in order, anchored to a live element.
kind   identity, and the save key. Must be unique within a level.
target what it points at: item | furn | door | lock | open | zoom | pan | shop | lastEl
when   the event that makes it eligible. Omit = show from level start.
until  the event that dismisses it. Omit = defaults to `kind`.
text   supports {container} {room} {item} {handSlots} {rowLen}
Events you can use for when/until: pickUp, place, goldPlace, open, door,
lock, zoom, pan, shop, rowComplete, contComplete, roomComplete.
3-2 and 4-2 deliberately have no tips — they are practice levels.
THEME IS THE OTHER HALF OF A LEVEL AND IT USED TO BE ALMOST ALWAYS "house".
Twenty-one of the first twenty-five jobs drew from the same fourteen rooms,
so by the midgame a player had seen the Attic and its two chests often enough
to name them, and the only relief was three dream levels. A theme is nearly
free — a room pool and three CSS variables — and the thing that was missing
was not more rooms, it was a REASON to be somewhere else. Clients are that
reason: the frat has a frat house, Zorb has a ship, the wizard has a tower,
the parrot has a zoo. Retheming their existing jobs cost seven words and
changed the shape of the whole midgame.
The house is still the tutorial (1-1 to 2-2) and still the ending, because
the late clients — a robot learning chores, a new father, a researcher who
hasn't looked up in three years — are all specifically domestic. What it is
no longer is the default.
A level's "rooms" may not exceed the room count of its theme; validate.js
checks it. The dream pool is 4, the new pools are 6 and 7.
"talents": false — this level has not met ⭐ yet, so it hands out none:
no reward chips, and no talent draft however many rows you finish. Stars
are still counted internally, so switching it on needs no migration.
It is set on every level BEFORE 5-1 "Talent Show", which is the level that
actually teaches stars and talents (see its tip and blurb). Without it the
first threshold, 4 ⭐, is crossed on the LAST item of 1-2 — the second level
of the game — and a modal asks the player to pick one of three talents they
have never heard of. Move the flag if you move where talents are taught.
"quests": false on 1-2 / 2-1 / 2-2. The quest seal starts a container
LOCKED, and the tutorial block runs contLocks: 0 on purpose — the first
locked thing in the game is meant to be 3-1, which is called Under Lock.
Without this the seal quietly put a locked cupboard in level two, four
levels early, before anything had taught what a lock is. Notes still drop
in these levels; with no seal, quests.js asks about an open container.
INSERTING IS SAFE — it did not used to be. Progress is saved as the SET of
finished level ids plus a frontier, not as an index into this array, so a
level dropped into the middle shows up as playable-but-unplayed and nothing
downstream re-locks. See LEGACY_ORDER in js/config.js, which is the frozen
22-id order the old integer saves migrate through and must never be edited.
Two rules survive: every level must be claimed by exactly one client stage
in clients.json, and an `id` here must never be REUSED for a different job,
because a player who finished the old one would find the new one already
done. `id` is the label; `blurb` is only used when no client says it aloud.

levels.name: Pick It Up

tips.text: Tap an item to pick it up
Drag items here to put them away
Now add all items to the {container}

levels.blurb: Three things on the floor, one home. Tap to grab, drag to place.

levels.name: Sort It Out

tips.text: Tap a container to look inside
Gold glow = it lives here. Grey shake = wrong home.

levels.blurb: Two homes now. Gold flash = right home. Cold = try again.

levels.name: Open Doors

tips.text: Tap the door to walk into the next room

levels.blurb: A second room. Your hands hold {handSlots} — plan the trip.

levels.name: Across the House

tips.text: Pinch or scroll to zoom in

levels.blurb: Three rooms of mess. The minimap remembers where you've been.

_note: FIRST DREAM. Placed here on purpose: you cannot dream about tidying
until you have tidied, and four jobs in is where a house starts to
look like the same house. It teaches nothing — the whole beat is
'where am I' — so quests: false, because the quest seal starts a
container LOCKED and the very next level, 3-1, is called Under Lock
and is where locks are supposed to arrive.
levels.name: The Sorting Dream
levels.blurb: You are asleep, and the sky is untidy.

levels.name: Under Lock

tips.text: This one's locked — drag a key 🔑 onto it

levels.blurb: One chest is locked. Find the keys 🔑 and drag them onto it.

levels.name: Hidden Stashes
levels.blurb: Two locked stashes this time. Keys open any lock.

levels.name: The Locked Door

tips.text: A locked door — the keys are on this side

levels.blurb: A whole room, sealed. The keys are always on your side of the door.

_note: The wizard arrives one job after the alien, on purpose. 4-1 is the first
time the game says 'this client is not a person' and T-1 is the second, so
the pair of them lands as a turn rather than as one oddity.
talents: false because 5-1 is still where stars are taught, and every level
before it has to stay quiet.
levels.name: Four Hundred Years
levels.blurb: Four hundred years in one tower and nothing thrown away.

levels.name: Full House
levels.blurb: Everything at once. Good luck out there.

levels._note: Locks and keys are taught by now (3-1, 4-1), so this one keeps its seal.
levels.name: The Comet Yard
levels.blurb: Ice in one place, rock in the other.

levels.name: Talent Show

tips.text: Tap here — this is what you've learned

levels.blurb: Finish rows to earn ⭐. Cross a threshold and you pick a new talent.

levels._note: First zoo job, and the first of the two arcs that argue with each other. Parrot opens; Boris answers three jobs later.
levels.name: Chain of Command
levels.blurb: The humans clock off at six. After six, somebody else is in charge.

levels.name: Friday Inspection
levels.blurb: Two locked chests and someone important arriving Friday.

levels.name: The Apprentice Problem
levels.blurb: Someone reorganised four hundred years of this. By colour.

levels.name: Boris Has A System
levels.blurb: The other one who runs this zoo, and the one who does the lifting.

levels.name: Field Report
levels.blurb: A sealed door, a locked chest, and someone taking notes.

levels.name: Deposit Day
levels.blurb: Five rooms, everything locked, and a landlord on the way.

levels.name: The Last Room
levels.blurb: The whole house, one last time.

levels._note: All four dream rooms at once — the pool is exactly 4, so this is the only dream level that never varies its rooms.
levels.name: Every Star A Home
levels.blurb: Every star has a home. It is never once finished.

levels.name: Everything I Have Ever Kept
levels.blurb: The tower is being inspected. That is not a figure of speech.

levels.name: Supervised Learning
levels.blurb: Someone is watching how you do this. Closely.

levels.name: The Banana Question
levels.blurb: Every banana in the facility is going somewhere. Somewhere is the vault.

levels.name: Nap Window
levels.blurb: Forty minutes. Maybe thirty.

levels.name: Training Data
levels.blurb: Everything in here has been sorted once already. Badly.

levels.name: Negotiation
levels.blurb: The bananas are gone. All of them. He counted twice.

levels.name: Peer Review
levels.blurb: Visitors on Thursday. Sealed doors today.

levels.name: Second Wind
levels.blurb: Every drawer in the house has been opened. None of them closed.

levels.name: Terms Agreed
levels.blurb: A functioning chain of command, at last, and twelve bananas a day.

levels.name: Confidence Interval
levels.blurb: A house nobody has seen before, and someone taking notes.

levels.name: The Sealed Wing
levels.blurb: Rooms that haven't been opened in three years.

levels._note: Six rooms out of a six-room pool, so this one never varies — the same trick D-3 pulls, and for the same reason: a finale should show you the whole world at once.
levels.name: Twelve A Day
levels.blurb: Best year this place has had. Don't tell him that.

levels.name: Sleeping Through
levels.blurb: Eight hours of sleep and a year of mess.

levels.name: Publication
levels.blurb: Eleven years of work, finished. Eleven years of everything else, not.
